correctness.rationale: PASS: A map with k cyclic points has probability a_{n,k} k/n with a=(n)_k/n^k, and its cyclic permutation is uniform; permutations with two cycles count (k-1)!H_{k-1}. This gives P(M=2)=Z_n/n and the exact conditional pair weights a/Z*[1/s+1/(k-s)] for 2s<k, or a/(Zs) for 2s=k (half correction). The Gaussian bound a<=exp(-k(k-1)/(2n)) and H_{k-1}=log k+O(1) yield Z_n~(I0/2)sqrt(n)log n. For k~x sqrt(n), s~y sqrt(n), local mass times log n has the stated two-dimensional Riemann intensity (2/I0)e^{-x²/2}(1/y+1/(x-y)); diagonal equal-cycle lattice has zero scaled macroscopic measure. Integrating y from a to x/2 yields log((x-a)/a) and Gaussian tails justify limit. For every fixed q>0, the endpoint singularity t^{q-1} is integrable, unnormalized k-moment scales k^q I_q, and Gaussian dominated Riemann sums give coefficient 2I_q mu_q. Variance uses squared mean lower order; tight k-window plus harmonic smaller-cycle law gives joint independent (|G|,U/2) logarithmic weak scale. Independent exact enumeration of all maps n=2..6 gave conditional stratum counts and probability formulas matching exactly; finite enumerations do not prove asymptotics.

The exact finite joint law and weak-scale observation are classical specializations, not asserted new.
